newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open higher.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open higher.

text.p: COMEX copper was called to open higher Thursday in line with firmer LME copper after Wednesday's swift rebound from Tuesday's selloff, traders said.
COMEX December copper was called unchanged to up 0.50 cent from Wednesday's close of 92.80 cents a lb. It traded from 92.05 to 93.40 on ACCESS.

COMEX copper warehouse stocks rose 947 short tons to 29,821 short tons Wednesday after a 1,390-short-ton rise Tuesday, with some of the gains believed to be transfers from the LME warehouse in Long Beach, Calif.
The COMEX December/March backwardation eased to 0.57 cent at Wednesday's close from a high of 3.00 cents Oct 25, suggesting prompt market tightness eased a little, traders said.

Meanwhile, open interest in COMEX copper rose in the past month to a peak of 61,113 Oct 25, the highest since June, which some analysts interpret as meaning, producers see recent gains as unsustainable requiring further hedging.
